messages:
incident-bot: SEV2 alert: Multiple containers reporting OOM / CUDA errors on pool-gpu-9. Starting incident channel. Please acknowledge.

maria.g: ack. seeing node flaps on 10.2.3.45, 10.2.3.47. Paged-attention allocator logs show repeated page faults.

raj.k: I see steady memory climb on kvcache: resident -> 95% over last 2 hours on affected pods. Not a single big spike, slow creep.

kevin.l: customer-ops pinged: one tenant reporting elevated latency and a handful of 5xx errors. Probably throttled fallback.

eng-runtime: collecting core dumps and CUDA driver traces now. initial `dmesg` shows "NVRM: GPU page fault" repeated.

maria.g: stack from allocator: ```
2026-03-17T01:12:43Z alloc/paged.cpp:423 free_slab: slab_count=0x7fffd, fragment_count=0x12
2026-03-17T01:12:44Z kv/cache.cpp:211 insert: cache_size=124GB target=64GB
```

raj.k: rolling a restart on pool-gpu-9 to stop immediate OOMs. Applying `kubectl rollout restart` on deployment/inference-paged-*. Doing sequential to avoid cluster-wide churn.

support-ops: Notified impacted tenant (acct-783). They report degraded inference for async batch jobs. No data loss, but jobs are timing out.

kevin.l: mitigation plan: 1) scale down worker concurrency on affected pods, 2) enable aggressive kv eviction TTL for night, 3) deploy temporary kernel knob `allocator.compact_threshold=0.65`. Anyone opposed?

maria.g: fine with plan. adding temporary trace flags: `--kv-debug=frag` and `--paged-tracer=on` to capture fragmentation metrics.

eng-runtime: uploaded driver logs and cuda backtraces to /tmp/inc614159. Attaching small excerpt: ``ERROR: cuCtxSynchronize() failed: CUDA_ERROR_OUT_OF_MEMORY at infer_loop.cu:128``

raj.k: after restart we saw two pods recover but one re-entered CrashLoopBackOff with OOM in post-start hook. grabbing logs.

maria.g: logs show heavy KV cache growth from prefixes for a single customer conversation pattern causing many small allocations and persistent page fragments. Suspect fragmentation during attention paging hot-path.

kevin.l: short-term: patch rollout to reduce kv prefetch window from 64 -> 16 for paged attention on affected model family. Will push canary to 1 pod in 60s.

support-ops: Customer wants ETA for full restore. We communicate: "mitigations in progress, likely restored for most workloads in ~30-45m, we will update in 15m".

eng-runtime: canary looks good, memory growth halted on that pod. Pushing to remaining pods in the pool with 1-min spacing.

raj.k: monitoring: adding alert to flag sustained RSS growth >5% over 10m for these deploys. Also scheduling a postmortem to figure fragmentation -> leak relationship.

maria.g: note for postmortem: capture exact input traffic causing KV cache churn, and KV slot allocation histogram. Also check CUDA driver version mismatch possibility — two nodes had driver 525.x vs rest 530.x.

kevin.l: agreed. Action items: (1) finish rollout and confirm customer latency back to baseline (assigned: raj.k), (2) collect artifact bundle and create incident page (assigned: eng-runtime), (3) temporary cluster policy to isolate pool-gpu-9 from autoscaler for next 24h (assigned: maria.g).

maria.g: added temporary policy and bumped quota for pool-gpu-9. continuing to monitor.

support-ops: update to customer: "we completed mitigations; we're monitoring for reoccurrence and will follow up with a root-cause within 48h." :thumbsup:

incident-bot: incident status updated to: Mitigated (partial). Next update in 15m or on significant change.

kevin.l: thanks team. I'll start the RCA doc and ping for timeline once we have full artifact bundle.

maria.g: nightshift triage handed off to oncall-uk for watch. leaving notes in pagerduty.

eng-runtime: last check: no new OOMs in 20m. closing on-call loop for immediate emergency.

raj.k: recording for postmortem: likely root causes: allocator fragmentation due to small persistent KV slots + mixed driver versions exacerbating page faults. Need long-term fixes: defragmenter, stronger eviction policy, and upgrade policy for drivers.

support-ops: acknowledged. moving to incident follow-up channel."
